title: Attested scope migration does not carry code-source locality cutover state or close the code bridge
wanted_capability: An operator-attested relpath-move (blackbox project-catalog scope-migrate --operator-attested) on a project governed by the code-source locality cutover should leave the daemon bootable. Today the migration rewrites the catalog scope and opens a code bridge, but the checksummed code-source and blame locality cutover markers keep their rows at the old scope and the current generation stays keyed on the old scope, so verify_live fails closed at boot in sequence: first "governed project must retain producer" (row scope no longer matches catalog scope), then after a row rewrite "invalid row" (nested generation and observation scopes must agree), then "no longer has a current generation from its cutover authority" (generation still under the old scope). The reverse migration is refused while the bridge is open, and the bridge can only close through new-scope activation, which needs the daemon up. Wanted: the migration transaction should either rewrite or tombstone the project's locality rows (with recomputed checksum) and treat the pre-migration generation as an activation in flight until the first publish under the new scope, or refuse the migration up front for a governed project with a pointer to the bridge-aware sequence. Same family as the retirement discharge gap.
missing_primitive: a locality-marker rewrite or tombstone stage in the scope-migration transaction, plus bridge-aware boot verification for a migrated governed project
fallback_used: Manual maintenance-pod repair with the daemon stopped: removed the migrated project's row from both locality markers with recomputed checksums (backups kept on the state volume), matching how post-cutover onboarded projects carry no row; the collector's first publish under the new scope is expected to close the bridge. Roughly 25 minutes of corpus daemon downtime.
evidence: sibling gap-7e4c11ce (retirement does not discharge locality marker rows)
